posts.text: @RoyD I agree that working capital and cash conversion are important areas to watch. However, I think it is worth looking at the current cash flow situation in the context of where the company is in its growth journey. Harshdeep is still a relatively young listed company that is investing for growth. Over the last few years, it has expanded its manufacturing capacity, increased its product portfolio, entered new categories such as outdoor furniture and shade nets, strengthened exports, and expanded its distribution network. posts.text: I think my only gripe here is that it’s a business where cashflows are currently getting locked in working capital requirements. FCF is currently negative and any issues with trade partners and cost of inputs will cause this to decline. I understand the Capex is high right now and is probably a good thing but even on the Operating level cash flows seem slim. Scaling will be a challenge.
